pages.text: Sunlight fell on the paper window. "Morning, Kota," Dad called. Kota wriggled like a caterpillar under the quilt. "A little longer..."
By the time Kota got up, the sun was high and the steam looked dull. Dad had done the cleaning alone.
An elderly owl came back from his nighttime walk, ready for bed. "We keep opposite hours!" He laughed.
Dad said, "Tomorrow, let's find the first steam. It's a treasure that only appears for a little while in the morning."
The next morning, Kota opened their eyes, stretched, and hopped out of bed. Even the sun looked half asleep.
The first steam puffed up in the morning light. Pink clouds floated like blossoms over the baths.
Dad and Kota watched side by side. The owl stopped on his way to bed. "Beautiful!" Kota's tail lifted.
"Only early risers get to see it?" "It's a morning gift," Dad said. Kota felt proud to have received one.
"One, open my eyes! Two, stretch! Three, welcome the steam!" Kota practiced their morning steps.
That evening, Dad hugged Kota as they lay down early. The day had felt so long and full. Under the quilt, Kota whispered, "Puffy clouds, the first steam!"
